events.title: CDC rescinds embargo on importation of civets and Family Viverridae
events.summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention rescinded its 21-year embargo on the importation of civets and all members of the Family Viverridae (genets, binturong, and related species) into the United States, effective immediately. The embargo, originally imposed in January 2004 following the SARS outbreak, was based on the assumption that civets were a reservoir host for SARS-CoV-1. CDC determined the import restriction no longer serves public health interests and the marginal benefit does not outweigh the burden on importers.
